fixes.summary: a React commit re-applies captured import metadata only for the subtree it changed, instead of walking the whole captured document (~44 ms per commit on a large materialized editor)

a metadata pass filters each node's children once and resolves each captured binding once, instead of re-walking every binding's path from the root in each filter and loop (a scoped pass on one shipped editor: 13-15 ms -> 1.5 ms)
a metadata pass applies a given face to a given native Label once, however many captured text bindings resolve to it

a commit that changes only a data-* attribute no captured-state or runtime selector names runs no metadata pass and does not bump the mutation epoch (a hover marker cost ~1.8 ms of metadata pass plus ~2.9 ms of captured-state rescanning per hover on one shipped editor)

a colour/opacity/fill/stroke-only commit is paint-only: where the capture owns that channel on that node the runtime restores just that property, instead of re-running the metadata pass over the subtree and bumping the mutation epoch

the setState calls one requestAnimationFrame or timer callback makes commit once when it returns, instead of once per call under LegacyRoot (one editor's post-mount state hydrate made 13 commits from a single animation frame, ~380 ms of its editor-open settle)

a metadata pass reads every layout binding's box metrics before writing any captured geometry, and measures text targets once after all writes, so it lays the tree out twice per pass instead of once per binding (78 layout passes to 2 on one shipped editor's first apply)

a re-render that only hands an event prop a new closure updates the handler registry and makes no bridge call, instead of re-arming and re-installing the native listener (six inline handlers cost 12 bridge calls per commit)

fontSize, letterSpacing and lineHeight strings resolve px, em, rem, % and normal to pixels before the bridge, instead of reaching it as a bare leading number ('0.08em' became 0.08 px, '6px' line height became 6x the font size)

a style key that disappears from a commit, or becomes null, hands its native slots back to the widget's starting value (layout through resetStyleProperty), instead of only ten keys resetting and an active-only bold, shadow, scale or padding staying painted after the conditional spread drops it
